Subject: Post-call recap: context length profiling + pricing follow-up

Hi Olivia (and Tom),

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking us through the editor/export flows and the analytics use case. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a tailored pricing + config recommendation: 

1) What we heard as the primary constraints:
- Most interactive sessions are short (FAQ/chat), but you also have a long-form export flow for analytics reports.
- Latency requirement: P95 < 800ms for interactive; long-form exports can be async.

2) What we need from you to finalize the pricing estimate: (please reply inline if easier)
- Avg prompt tokens per request (example: 200)
- Avg completion tokens per request (example: 400)
- Monthly token volume (prompt + completion combined) or range (low/typical/high)
- Percentage of requests that need >8k context / >32k context / >128k context (approx)
- Target $/1M tokens (if you have a target unit-economics target) or monthly budget range for the inference layer
- Any SLOs for throughput/concurrency we should assume for Dedicated (or hosted) pricing

I've attached a basic pricing worksheet (acme-pricing-sheet-v1.pdf) and a sample CSV format (context-length-samples.csv) you can fill if easier.

Next steps: if you can share the token averages + volume, I’ll send back 2 configurations: 1) lowest-cost hosted plan with batching/quantization suggestions and 2) Dedicated estimate (reserved capacity) with expected unit $/1M tokens for 8k vs 32k contexts. If that looks good we can schedule a short follow-up (30 min) to review.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Answers below (we pulled a 30-day sample from our logs):

- Avg prompt tokens: 220 (median 180)
- Avg completion tokens: 480 (median 300)
- Monthly token volume (30-day): ~40M tokens total (prompt+completion). Typical range: 25M - 60M.
- Percent of requests needing extended context:
  - >8k context: ~5% (mostly long exports and multi-document analytics prompts)
  - >32k context: ~0.2% (very rarely for monthly consolidated reports)
  - >128k context: 0% currently, but we may have a quarterly export that could approach 200k tokens in the future
- Target unit economics: we're aiming for ~$60 / 1M tokens for inference (prompt+completion combined) as a target for a deal to be budget-friendly for our finance team.
- Concurrency: interactive traffic peaks at ~60 QPS, but bursts are short (1-2 mins). Long-form exports run in batch jobs overnight and can be queued.

We attached the sample CSV filled with a few representative rows — let me know if you need per-route breakdowns.

Tom and I are generally leaning toward a Dedicated reserve if the unit economics for 32k contexts are reasonable. Happy to review your 8k vs 32k cost delta.

Best,
Olivia

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: context length profiling + pricing follow-up

Olivia — really helpful, thank you. Based on your numbers here's a concise recommendation and the pricing deltas: 

Summary of your traffic (30d sample):
- Avg prompt: 220 tokens; avg completion: 480 tokens; combined ~700 tokens/request.
- Monthly volume range: 25M - 60M tokens. Baseline 40M tokens.
- Extended context usage: 5% >8k, 0.2% >32k, 0% >128k (with possible future quarterly spikes).

Quick unit economics (ballpark):
- Hosted (8k contexts, optimized quantized model): Estimated $85 / 1M tokens. This uses aggressive batching + prefix caching for interactive flows; long-form exports would be async.
- Dedicated (8k contexts, reserved capacity): Estimated $60 / 1M tokens at 40M/mo usage with a 12-month commit (includes 10% volume-based discount).
- Dedicated (32k contexts, reserved capacity, larger GPU types + KV cache tuning): Estimated $95 / 1M tokens at same commit level — higher due to memory footprint and lower GPU utilization for many short requests.

Given your target ~$60 / 1M tokens, the Dedicated 8k configuration is within range with a modest commit. For the 32k need, we have two options to hit closer to $60:
1) Hybrid routing: serve 95% of traffic on 8k-optimized instances and route the 5% long exports to a smaller pool of 32k instances (effectively reducing the overall blended unit cost).
2) Engineering optimizations: pre-chunking the quarterly export and doing streaming/iterative aggregation to avoid huge KV cache pressure (this can materially reduce the cost of the 32k path).

Attachments: I attached an updated estimate (redwood-estimate-acme-v2.pdf) with line-item pricing and recommended autoscale settings. I've also put a draft mutual action plan in the Drive link (see thread metadata link).

Next steps:
- If Acme is comfortable, we can prepare a Dedicated proposal with a 12-month commit and the hybrid routing config.
- I propose a 30-min tech + finance sync with Tom and your infra lead to validate SLOs and expected export behavior. Available Thu 3/12 or Fri 3/13 morning PST — which works for you?

If that aligns, I’ll pull Rishi in to scope the paperwork and discount approvals.

Thanks — Marissa
